title: fastpath-runtime-sync-brief-scratchpad
content:
Purpose: quick, focused sync with the serving runtime/infra/console triad. This is my personal prep for the recurring fastpath sync slot (Mon mornings, 30m). The goal: unblock rollout blockers, flag production regressions, align on next-step owners, and make sure console telemetry surfaces the right signals.

Meeting context (short):
- Post-canary rollout of v2.3 kernel selection landed last week; latency baseline looks good but we see a tail in 99th percentile on long context (>6k).
- Autoscaler tuned to new batching profile; some teams reported degraded cold-start times for small requests.
- Console traces missing structured fields for model-variant when fallback to quantized path occurs — hurts postmortem.

Agenda (25–30m):
1) Quick round (2m each): hot items from SRE, Serving, Console (status + one ask)
2) Latency tails on long-context flows (8m): data, hypothesized causes, immediate mitigations
3) Autoscaler/cold-start observations (6m): perf guardrails vs batching economics
4) Console telemetry gap for model-variant on fallback (6m): short product asks + tracking
5) Action-item recap + owners (3m)

Notes to self (things to surface):
- Bring the p99/p999 sparkline for last 72h (filtered by route: /v1/generate, seq_len>4096). Quick filter query: prod.traces.service:runtime AND request.seq_len:>4096 AND env:prod.
- Show two examples of requests hitting fallback quantized kernel with timestamps + trace ids (so console/serving can correlate).
- Call out recent autoscaler policy change: pause_threshold lowered from 60s -> 30s; explain rationale and surface side-effects.

Open questions / hypotheses: 
- Hypothesis A: KV cache eviction policy combined with long-context kernel choice causing repeated recomputation at step transitions. Check cache hit-rate per model variant across long sessions.
- Hypothesis B: New kernel selection path introduces small scheduling jitter that compounds for sequences >4k on A100s under high concurrency. Need microbenchmark.
- Question for Console: can we add model_variant and kernel_name as indexed fields (low-cardinality) in the trace event to allow quick filtering? What is cost/retention impact?

Action items (working, with owners and suggested due dates):
- SOF-1: Export and attach 72h p99/p999 sparkline + two trace IDs for fallback cases to the meeting thread. Owner: Sofia Chen. Due: 2026-03-11. Status: in_progress.
- MAY-2: Run microbench of kernel scheduling under synthetic long-context workloads (4k, 6k, 8k) at low/medium/high concurrency, capture latencies. Owner: Maya Patel. Due: 2026-03-13. Status: todo.
- LIAM-3: Reopen autoscaler rollout PR to add a temporary 45s buffer for small-request pools and post a short rollout plan. Owner: Liam Brooks. Due: 2026-03-12. Status: todo.
- CONSOLE-4: Spike to add model_variant + kernel_name tags to runtime trace schema (prototype change + cost estimate). Owner: Console infra (cc: Priya, Lin). Due: 2026-03-18. Status: todo.
- SRE-5: Add an alert for KV cache miss amplification: trigger when per-session cache misses exceed 20% for >5m on any pool. Owner: Oncall SRE (Samir). Due: 2026-03-15. Status: proposed.

Prep checklist (what I'll bring to the sync):
- Quick slide (single page) with: one-liner problem statement, 3 charts (p99 sparkline, cache hit-rate by variant, microbench plan outline)
- Links to PRs and traces (attached in linked_artifacts)
- Two candidate mitigations: (1) conservative kernel pin for sessions >6k for 24h, (2) temporarily raise autoscaler buffer for small-request pool

Conversation prompts (concise):
- To Serving: if we pin kernel for long sessions, what rollback/compat risk? Any memory overhead?
- To Infra: do we have a lightweight way to sample full input sequences for affected traces without PII leakage?
- To Console: if cost estimate for index fields is >$X/month, what minimal subset of traces do we need to still be actionable?

Post-meeting follow-up template (for the thread):
- Summary: 2–3 bullet recap of decisions
- Action items: list owner/due/status
- Required approvals: list (if kernel pin or autoscaler buffer change needs ProdEng sign-off)
- Next check-in: tentative slot + criteria to close the ticket

Personal notes / friction items to remember: 
- Keep language non-blame in the meeting (facts + measurable metrics).
- If we can't get console indexing approved quickly, push for temporary manual correlation steps and set a follow-up to scope cost properly.
- Track any customer-facing incidents that might need comms. If any customer SLA affected, escalate to CS immediately.

Misc scratch lines (brain dump):
- Consider short-lived canary of kernel pin on 10% of capacity for sessions that start with seq_len>6k and have >1s initial latency spike.
- Might be worth correlating with model versions (v2.3 vs v2.2); add to microbench matrix.
- Note: remind release-engineering to freeze model-variant renaming during this troubleshooting window to avoid confusion in traces.

End of scratchpad. Will trim down before posting meeting invite notes.
